title: AP Statistics Unit 5 topic 5.1, seed A
stem: A researcher records (hours of sunlight, daily plant growth) for five independent observations: (2, 3), (4, 6), (6, 9), (8, 12), (10, 2). The first quantity is used to explain the second. Which description of the scatterplot is best supported?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Put daily plant growth on the horizontal axis and hours of sunlight on the vertical axis; the last point proves that the response causes the explanatory variable.
choices.rationale: The variables were recorded as explanatory then response; exchanging the axes changes the intended prediction, and a scatterplot alone does not establish causation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The association is negative and roughly linear because the final response is smaller than the first response.
choices.rationale: The direction of the main pattern comes from all observations rather than comparing only the first and last response values.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Put hours of sunlight on the horizontal axis and daily plant growth on the vertical axis; four points follow a positive, roughly linear pattern, with the last point unusually low.
choices.rationale: Correct: The explanatory variable is the first coordinate. The first four response values rise with x; the fifth lies well below that pattern. One unusual point does not reverse the four-point direction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No pattern is visible because one unusual point cancels the consistent increase in the other four observations.
choices.rationale: The first four points form a visible positive pattern; the unusual fifth point should be named rather than erasing that pattern.

title: AP Statistics Unit 5 topic 5.2, seed A
stem: In a sample, the correlation between distance in miles and delivery time is +0.78. An analyst converts the first variable to a new unit using a positive scale factor, then reports the negative of the second variable instead. Which statement is justified about the new correlation and a possible causal claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new correlation is -0.78; the sign reverses because one variable was negated, and neither correlation establishes causation.
choices.rationale: Correct: A positive rescaling preserves r=+0.78; multiplying one variable by -1 changes its sign to -0.78. Association alone cannot prove causation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The new correlation is +0.78; changing units and negating a variable cannot change correlation's direction.
choices.rationale: Positive rescaling preserves correlation, but negating one of the variables reverses its sign.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The new correlation is -0.78; its magnitude establishes that changing distance in miles causes a change in delivery time.
choices.rationale: The sign calculation is right, but the size of a correlation does not by itself identify a causal effect.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The new correlation is 0 because both variables were transformed before it was computed.
choices.rationale: Linear transformations do not in general destroy association; a positive rescaling and a sign reversal leave the magnitude unchanged.

title: AP Statistics Unit 5 topic 5.3, seed A
stem: A linear model fitted using practice sessions from 1 to 10 predicts score points by y-hat=42+4x. What should an analyst report for x=12?

choices.rationale: Correct: Substitute x=12: 42+4(12)=90. Since 12>10, the prediction extrapolates; the equation yields a value but reliability is weaker outside the data range.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The model predicts 90 score points, and this is interpolation because the equation accepts x=12.
choices.rationale: A fitted equation can be evaluated outside the observed x-range, but that use is extrapolation, not interpolation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The model predicts 50 score points, since the model input must be the distance past the largest observed x.
choices.rationale: The model uses the actual explanatory value x, not the distance past the edge of the data range.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No predicted value can be calculated once x lies outside the observed range.
choices.rationale: Extrapolation is less reliable, yet the model still produces a numerical prediction when x is substituted.

title: compare residual diagnostics across models
stem: Two candidate models predict energy use from temperature. At five increasing x-values, model A has residuals [3, 1, -2, 1, 3], and model B has residuals [1, -1, 0, 1, -1]. Which judgment about form follows from these residuals?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Model B has the more appropriate form for energy use: A leaves a systematic curve across temperature, whereas B's residuals fluctuate around zero.
choices.rationale: Correct: Model A's endpoint and middle residuals trace a repeated high-low-high or low-high-low shape. B's signs fluctuate without that curve; zero residual at every point is unnecessary.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Model A has the better form for energy use because an orderly curve of residuals is desirable.
choices.rationale: The orderly curve is evidence that A misses systematic structure, not evidence in its favor.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both forms are equally supported because each list contains positive and negative residuals.
choices.rationale: Having both signs is not enough; the order of residuals across x reveals A's pattern.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither form can be used because a fitted model must make every residual exactly zero.
choices.rationale: Residuals need not all be zero for a model to be useful; random scatter is the relevant form check.
